title: The Portrait of Cold Spring
premise: Isandro Fairweather, a meticulous property surveyor, is hired to appraise Cold Spring House, a derelict estate whose founders built it as a vessel for a ritual that binds the town's dead to its walls. His sleep recordings begin capturing a second voice answering his spoken questions, and he realizes the house is appraising him in return—measuring whether he is worthy to complete what the founders left unfinished. As Isandro uncovers records of previous surveyors who vanished mid-appraisal, he falls for Mara Voss, the town archivist hiding her own family's role in the ritual. In the end, Isandro must choose between documenting the truth and destroying it: he finishes the founders' ritual with himself as the final entry, sealing the house's hunger but erasing every record—including his own name—from existence, leaving only Mara's memory and one impossible photograph.
about_author: Elodie Dunmore is the pen name of a former land registry clerk from upstate New York who spent a decade cataloguing deeds for houses no one would buy twice. Her fiction explores the quiet horror of paperwork, inheritance, and the things buildings remember when people won't.

chapters.title: The Appraisal Clause
chapters.summary: Isandro arrives at Cold Spring House with his instruments, checklists, and recording equipment, treating the assignment as routine. The house's dimensions don't reconcile—interior measurements exceed exterior by eleven feet. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: professional calm masking the first hairline crack of unease.

chapters.title: Eleven Feet of Nowhere
chapters.summary: Isandro remeasures obsessively, documenting the discrepancy in triplicate, but the extra footage shifts each day. He finds a founder's ledger hidden in a wall cavity, written in surveyor's notation—the same system he uses. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: fascination curdling into recognition; the house speaks his language.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: In town, Isandro meets Mara Voss at the historical society, who warns him off the property without explanation. Their chemistry is immediate and guarded; she recognizes the founder's ledger and goes pale. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: warmth and attraction shadowed by her fear, the first thread of loyalty vs. truth.

chapters.title: First Night Recording
chapters.summary: Isandro sleeps in the house to monitor temperature anomalies. Playback reveals a second voice—a woman's—answering his sleep-murmured questions with unnerving accuracy about the house's history. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into methodological resolve; documentation as prayer begins in earnest.

chapters.title: Questions Answered
chapters.summary: Isandro deliberately asks questions aloud before sleeping. The voice names the founders—Aldous and Verity Crane—and says the house is 'counting him.' The recordings show timestamps during which he has no memory. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: the horror of being measured, of invisibility failing.

chapters.title: What Mara Keeps
chapters.summary: Mara shows Isandro sealed town records: four surveyors appraised Cold Spring House over 140 years; none filed final reports or were seen again. Her grandmother was a Crane descendant sworn to maintain the estate's 'accounts.' POV: Mara. Emotional beat: guilt and duty warring with her growing love for Isandro.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Deciphering the ledger, Isandro learns the Cranes bound something into the house—a debt collected in appraisals—and the ritual requires a surveyor to 'close the account' before the centennial date, six weeks away. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: dread of purpose; he wasn't hired by accident.

chapters.title: Rooms That Rehearse
chapters.summary: Isandro finds furnished rooms behind the missing square footage: tableaux of past surveyors' final nights, frozen mid-action, including one holding a camera. The house is rehearsing his ending. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: violation and vertigo; his documentation now documents him.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Mara confesses her family kept the house fed with names for generations, and that she was instructed to befriend any surveyor—to keep him compliant until the centennial. She swears she refused. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: love against duty made explicit; Isandro must decide whether to believe her.

chapters.title: The Voice Has a Name
chapters.summary: Through the recordings, Isandro learns the second voice is Verity Crane, bound alive into the walls in 1924, still keeping accounts. She begs him—not to free her, but to finish the ritual properly, or the house will take the whole town. POV: alternating Isandro/Verity (via transcript). Emotional beat: pity entangled with manipulation; can a prisoner be trusted?

chapters.title: Interlude: The Town That Forgets
chapters.summary: Isandro walks Cold Spring village and notices residents can't recall the missing surveyors' faces, though their offices remain untouched. The house's appetite extends outward. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: isolation deepening; the truth has no witnesses left.

chapters.title: Mara's Grandmother
chapters.summary: Mara confronts her dying grandmother, who reveals the ritual's true cost: the closing surveyor becomes the new permanent resident, replacing Verity. The family's loyalty was always a chain passed down. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: grief and fury; she realizes loving Isandro means sentencing him.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Verity offers Isandro an alternative: falsify the appraisal, declare the house sound, and walk away—but the debt will then collect from the town, starting with Mara's bloodline. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: temptation of self-preservation against love; the blurb's promise comes due.

chapters.title: Burn the Records
chapters.summary: Isandro attempts to destroy the ledger and recordings, believing ignorance might starve the house. The fire refuses to catch; ash reforms into notation on his own skin. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: futility and bodily horror; documentation cannot be undone, only completed.

chapters.title: What the House Wants
chapters.summary: Verity explains the full ritual: a willing surveyor must appraise the house honestly—every room, every room behind the rooms—and sign the final page. Honesty is the mechanism; the house feeds on accurate witness. POV: Verity. Emotional beat: terrible clarity; the trap was precision all along.

chapters.title: Mara's Choice
chapters.summary: Mara offers herself in Isandro's place, invoking a forgotten clause allowing a Crane descendant to close the account. The house rejects her—her loyalty is inherited, not chosen, and the ritual demands freely given witness. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: sacrifice refused; love proven real by its uselessness.

chapters.title: The Full Inventory
chapters.summary: Isandro begins the complete appraisal: three days walking every space, including the rehearsal rooms, narrating everything aloud while Verity answers. Each truthful observation transfers weight from her chains to his. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: solemnity and mounting dissolution; he is becoming legible to the house.

chapters.title: The Last Page
chapters.summary: At the centennial hour, Isandro signs the founders' ledger. Verity's voice unravels into gratitude and warning; the rehearsal rooms collapse inward. Mara holds his hand through the final measurement—he is now both appraiser and property. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: climax; devotion rendered as signature.

chapters.title: Sound and Empty Rooms
chapters.summary: Dawn. The house stands ordinary, correctly dimensioned, cold. Mara searches every room calling Isandro's name; the walls answer with silence that feels, briefly, like breath. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: desolate aftermath; victory indistinguishable from loss.

chapters.title: The Unwritten Man
chapters.summary: Town records show no surveyor ever visited Cold Spring House. Mara alone remembers, and her memories are already fraying at the edges. She finds Isandro's car gone, his hotel reservation never made. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: gaslit grief; memory as the last unreliable archive.

chapters.title: One Photograph
chapters.summary: Among Mara's digitized files survives a single image: Isandro at the threshold, timestamped though nothing else about him remains. When she speaks to the photograph at night, sometimes the exposure lightens, as if listening. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: fragile hope; love outlasting documentation.

chapters.title: Cold Spring, Warm
chapters.summary: Years later, Mara restores the house as a museum, telling visitors a story no record supports. On quiet evenings a second voice joins hers in empty rooms, patient and kind, keeping gentle accounts. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; some truths survive only as devotion.
